What We Do

Consulting Services Built Around Your Credit

Every client starts with a complete analysis. From there, we build a dispute and rebuilding plan for your personal credit, your business credit — or both.

Personal Credit Analysis

A line-by-line review of your reports from Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion. We flag every error, negative item, and score factor — then explain exactly what can be challenged and what to rebuild first.

Business Credit Analysis

A full review of your business credit profile and the personal credit behind it. We help owners separate, correct, and strengthen their profiles so the business is ready for vendor accounts, credit lines, and funding.

Hard Inquiry Removal

Too many hard inquiries drag your score down and scare off lenders. We review every inquiry on your reports and dispute the ones that were unauthorized, duplicated, or cannot be verified.

Personal Information Correction

Wrong names, old addresses, incorrect employers, and mixed personal data make your file a magnet for errors — and a risk for identity mix-ups. We work to remove and correct personal information that is wrong or doesn't belong to you.

Removal of Unverifiable Information

Under federal law, items on your credit report must be accurate and verifiable. If a bureau or furnisher can't verify an item, we challenge it and push for its removal — collections, late payments, charge-offs, and more.

Credit Building & Consulting

Removing negatives is only half the job. We coach you on utilization, positive tradelines, payment habits, and a step-by-step plan to build a stronger score — and keep it there.

Dispute & Removal

What We Challenge On Your Reports

If an item is inaccurate, incomplete, outdated, or cannot be verified, it should not be hurting your credit. Here is what we review and dispute on your behalf:

  • Unauthorized hard inquiriesInquiries you never approved, duplicates, and inquiries a company cannot verify.
  • Unverifiable accounts & itemsAny listing the bureau or furnisher cannot document and verify.
  • Wrong personal informationIncorrect names, old or wrong addresses, wrong employers, and other people's data mixed into your file.
  • Collections & charge-offsIncluding paid items still reporting incorrectly and accounts that aren't yours.
  • Late payments reported in errorPayments marked late when they weren't, or reported on the wrong account.
  • Duplicate & re-aged accountsThe same debt listed twice, or old debts made to look new.
  • Identity theft & mixed-file itemsAccounts and inquiries that belong to someone else or came from fraud.
  • Outdated negative itemsNegative information reporting past the legal reporting period.
Straight talk: No company can legally remove accurate, verified information from your credit report — and we won't promise that. What we do is enforce your rights under the Fair Credit Reporting Act: every item on your report must be accurate, complete, and verifiable, and we challenge every item that isn't.

Questions

Before You Get Started

Can you remove hard inquiries from my credit?

We review every hard inquiry on your reports. Inquiries that were unauthorized, duplicated, or cannot be verified can be disputed with the bureaus. Inquiries you did authorize and that are accurate generally stay for up to two years — we'll tell you honestly which ones can be challenged.

What does "unverifiable information" mean?

When you dispute an item, the bureau must investigate and the furnisher must be able to verify the information is accurate and complete. If they can't verify it, it must be corrected or removed. A large share of our work is identifying items that fail that test.

Why does my personal information on my credit report matter?

Wrong names, old addresses, and someone else's data on your file can cause mixed files, mismatched accounts, and even identity-theft confusion. Cleaning up your personal information makes your whole report more accurate — and your disputes more effective.

Do you work on business credit too?

Yes. We analyze business credit profiles alongside the owner's personal credit, and consult on separating and building business credit so your company can qualify for accounts and funding on its own strength.

How long does the process take?

Bureaus typically have 30–45 days to investigate each dispute round. Timelines vary by how many items are on your reports and how the bureaus respond — during your free analysis, we'll give you a realistic picture for your situation.

Can anyone guarantee a specific score or deletion?

No — and be careful with anyone who does. Federal law prohibits guaranteeing results or removing accurate, verified information. What we guarantee is the work: a thorough analysis, properly documented disputes, and experienced guidance from a team doing this since 2005.
